name: MEET ME ON THE BRIDGE
notes: Kwai/Brooklyn/Mackinac ('Big Mac', ~5 mi, joins the peninsulas) all verified; softened the $1600 to 'Legend says' since the Sighs name is Byron's 19th-century invention, not documented convict behavior.

name: BUILT TO IMPRESS
notes: Astrodome-as-first-domed-stadium and Flatiron 1902/iron namesake verified; rewrote the $800 to describe Dr. King's 1963 speech instead of quoting the copyrighted line.

name: OUT ON THE BRINY
notes: Changed 'this lake in northern Israel' to 'this sea' (a briny category shouldn't call it a lake, and a lake category sits two slots away) and marked the Aegeus story as Greek myth rather than fact.

name: AT THE LAKE
notes: Loch Ness 1934 photo, Michigan as the only wholly-U.S. Great Lake, Great Salt Lake naming Salt Lake City, Speke's Lake Victoria all check; textbook gentle climb.

name: WEATHER OR NOT
notes: Replaced the Oz $800 because 'twister'/'cyclone' are equally correct responses to it — new hail clue has one answer; hurricane/typhoon, barometer and nor'easter naming verified.

name: TURN, TURN, TURN
notes: Solstice, Groundhog Day, Indian summer and the harvest moon (full moon nearest the equinox) all correct; only nit is 'summer' appearing in two responses.

name: A SUNDAY STROLL
notes: Central Park's 843 acres, Boston Common as oldest U.S. public park with cows banned in 1830, Kew's Palm House all verified; Giverny is the file's stiffest $2000 but Monet plus Normandy makes it a fair swing.

name: IRON HORSES
notes: Promontory 1869, Casey Jones 1900, Glenn Miller's 1941 hit and Pullman's Illinois works all check; 'track 29' is a factual detail, not a lyric quotation.

name: THE SHIP'S LOG
notes: Santa Maria's Christmas 1492 grounding, Constitution 1797, Monitor vs. Merrimack 1862 and Kon-Tiki's crew of six all correct; strongest ladder in the file.

name: THE GRAND TOUR
notes: Blarney, Salisbury Plain, Pamplona and the Lorelei Rhine all sound; 'stone' in the Blarney clue is the intended nudge, and Stonehenge only collides with the Fresh pack, not Easy.

name: TRUE NORTH
notes: CN Tower's 1,815 ft, Toronto as largest city, PEI as smallest province (by both area and population) and the 1898 Klondike rush all verified.

name: SOUTH OF THE BORDER
notes: Tenochtitlan under Mexico City, La Quebrada, Nov. 2 Day of the Dead and El Castillo's 91 steps per side all confirmed; gentle throughout.
